summary: High 5xx rate for tenant during keystore rollover causing runtime socket backlog and API 5xx wave
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Cobalt Health began reporting elevated 5xx rates for inference requests starting ~2026-03-11 03:20 UTC. Errors were mostly 502/503 returned by the Redwood API gateway. Customer impact: production traffic for 6 app routes experienced 30-60% failure rate for ~90 minutes during the window.

Impact:
- Affected customer: Cobalt Health (enterprise).
- Duration: ~03:20-04:50 UTC on 2026-03-11 (partial degradation continued intermittently until mitigations applied).
- User-visible: failed streaming sessions, aborted responses, HTTP 5xx to SDKs.

Timeline (initial):
- 03:15 UTC: Scheduled keystore rotation for platform-wide certs started (rolling across nodes).
- 03:18 UTC: First customer report via support channel (#support).
- 03:20 UTC: API gateway 5xx spike begins; alerts for apigw.error_rate and runtime.request_failures fire.
- 03:40 UTC: SRE engaged; initial mitigation attempts (temporary route drain) had limited effect.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region, tenant pinned to dedicated pool.
- Runtime version: 2026.02.7-serv-rt
- API gateway: apigw-1.12.0

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Trigger keystore rotation (rolling cert refresh) during sustained traffic.
2) A subset of gateway->runtime mutual-TLS handshakes fail transiently for seconds on a node during rotation.
3) Failed handshakes cause connection resets; gateway retries; runtime prefetch queue continues to accept upstream prefetch work.
4) Runtime listener accept queue length and socket_fd count climb; new connections hit backlog limits and are rejected, resulting in 502/503 responses.

Observed behavior & evidence:
- apigw metrics: apigw.error_rate spiked from baseline 0.7% to 42% for affected routes (charts linked below).
- runtime metrics: runtime.listener.backlog_spike and runtime.fd_count rose concurrently with handshake failures.
- Kernel stats snapshot: somaxconn at default 128 on affected nodes; SYN backlog dropped; no obvious OOM.
- TLS logs from gateway show short windows of "handshake failure: certificate not yet available" and "remote closed connection" timestamps matching spike.
- No core dumps found for the runtime; no immediate memory pressure.

Logs and dashboards (links):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/apigw/errors?from=2026-03-11T03:00Z&to=2026-03-11T05:00Z
- Kibana runtime logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/kibana/app/discover#runtime?query=SUP-233401
- Slack incident thread: #incidents -> message 1723

Temporary mitigations attempted:
- Disabled prefetch for affected tenant at 03:48 UTC (reduced downstream pressure).
- Put a routing rule to shift a portion of Cobalt Health traffic to a warm fallback pool at 03:52 UTC (partial recovery).
- Paused keystore rollout for the remainder of the region at 03:55 UTC.

Request from customer: Full post-incident analysis, permanent mitigation to prevent keystore rotations from causing availability loss, and guidance for tenant best practices during rotations.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: keystore rotation caused transient cert unavailability which produced TLS handshake failures between apigw and runtime. Unlike a pure TLS failure, runtime continued to accept prefetched work, so connection churn accumulated and hit accept/syn backlog limits.

What we checked:
- Verified rotation logs: keystore service restarted NodeAgent on each node to pick up new certs; restart window ~12s/node.
- Measured handshake failure ratio: ~7-12% of new handshakes to nodes in rotation window.
- FD counts: nodes under rotation showed fd_count climb from ~1200 to ~6600 over 10 minutes.
- somaxconn default 128 -> accept queue overflow.
- Autoscaler: did not trigger additional capacity because CPU and GPU utilization remained below scale-up thresholds; backlog buildup is a connection-level problem not CPU/GPU.

Hypotheses considered and ruled out:
- OOM or memory leak: no consistent memory growth; heaps stable.
- Model-level crash: runtime did not crash; returning 502s were at gateway/proxy level.

Actionable findings:
1) Keystore rotation implementation restarts local NodeAgent processes synchronously which interrupts TLS availability for short windows; when traffic is high, many nodes in quick succession produce repeated handshake failures.
2) The runtime's prefetch behavior accepts upstream work even while handshake failures are in progress, contributing to higher concurrent connections.
3) Kernel listen/accept backlog (somaxconn) is too low for the burst pattern produced by rotation failure/retries.

Suggested permanent fixes:
- Stagger keystore rotation: increase per-node delay and add health-check gating so NodeAgent only restarts after TLS socket drains.
- Treat handshake failures from internal mutual-TLS during rotation as 503-backoff signals to avoid aggressive retries in gateway.
- Add a temporary circuit-breaker on gateway for repeated "certificate unavailable" errors to fail fast and reduce connection churn.
- Increase somaxconn and ephemeral port tuning on runtime hosts as a safety buffer; coordinate with infra change window.
- Add a runtime config to refuse prefetch when inbound handshake error rate exceeds threshold.

Follow-ups created:
- ENG ticket to change keystore rollout logic and NodeAgent restart gating: INT-4367 (internal).
- Infra ticket to propose somaxconn bump and host tuning: INT-4419 (internal).
- Runbook update: add canary step and off-peak scheduling for keystore rollouts.
resolution:
Mitigations applied during incident:
- Paused keystore rotation across us-east-1 and completed a controlled staggered rollout during low-traffic window (completed 2026-03-12 02:20 UTC).
- Disabled prefetch for the affected tenant for the remainder of the high-traffic period; customer traffic returned to normal error rates by 04:10 UTC.
- Deployed temporary apigw rule to limit retries on TLS handshake failures (rolled in via github.com/redwood-inference/apigw/pull/2917).

Permanent remediation plan (in progress):
- INT-4367: Update NodeAgent to perform graceful TLS handoff and gating before restart (owner: infra-security). ETA: 2026-04-05.
- INT-4419: Coordinate with infra to raise somaxconn and tune net.core settings for runtime hosts. ETA: 2026-03-28.
- ENG: Add prefetch backpressure threshold tied to handshake error rate; PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4392.
- Update keystore rotation runbook and schedule canary rollouts with traffic-aware windows.

Customer-facing resolution notes sent to Cobalt Health at 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC. Customer confirmed service stability and accepted temporary mitigations; requested post-mortem and timeline for permanent fixes.
